reasoning: Xi Jinping has consolidated absolute control over the CCP, removed term limits, and faces no visible internal opposition or succession challenge. The political system is tightly controlled, and historical precedents show Chinese leaders rarely leave office prematurely except through death or major upheaval. A 7% probability over 18 months implies a roughly 1-in-14 chance, which is far too high given the current stability.
evidence_points: Xi removed presidential term limits in 2018 and secured a third term as General Secretary in 2022 with unanimous support.
No factional splits or public elite dissent have surfaced; the 20th Party Congress reinforced Xi’s dominance.
The timeline (July 2025–Dec 2026) is extremely short for a politically engineered removal absent an unexpected crisis.
Market overreaction to tail risk is common, but 7% implies an annualized exit probability unseen in modern Chinese history.
sources_consulted: Reports on CCP leadership transitions and 20th Party Congress outcomes
Analysis of Xi Jinping’s power consolidation since 2012
Historical data on Chinese General Secretary removal (none since 1980s)
